Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We're running a capex-forward budget this year and the exec team is asking whether Redwood can do a multi-year prepay with some built-in flexibility. Two specific asks from procurement and finance:

- Can we prepay for 36 months but defer up to 25% of annual committed tokens into a later year as a credit?
- If actual usage drops materially in year 2, are refunds allowed or do you only provide credits?

They also want to understand whether there is a pricing swingline: a short-term borrow of credits across quarters to smooth usage peaks without renegotiating.

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a quick forecast template and a draft SOW to show how we'd operationalize a swingline/credit approach (see attachments). High level proposal below:

- Term: 36 months, prepaid annually (customer prepays each 12-month tranche).
- Discounting: Effective discount applied to each prepaid tranche (tiered by size).
- Credit deferral: Up to 20% of each annual tranche can be deferred into a later year as an account credit, usable within the remaining term.
- Refunds: Refunds only for material contract breach; otherwise we offer credits against future usage.
- Swingline: A borrowing mechanism that allows one-quarter worth of credits to be shifted forward (max 25% of that quarter) with an automatic reconciliation at year-end; any shortfall billed at the overage blended rate.

Why these limits? They let Helios smooth short-term demand while preserving unit economics for Redwood. If you can share a 12-mo rolling forecast (monthly) we can stress-test the swingline exposure.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll get Ben to prep a pricing model (by end of day Monday).
2) Laura, can you sign off on the swingline/credit cap and the refund policy so I can send a consolidated counter to procurement?
3) Oliver — if that framework looks acceptable I’ll circulate a clean SOW for legal review.

Thanks,

Looping in pricing guidance. Quick read: the cap on deferral and swingline looks reasonable but I want to propose concrete discount numbers to make this actionable for procurement:

- If Helios prepays >= $750k per year: 15% discount on year 1 tranche, 12% on year 2, 10% on year 3.
- If they prepay >= $350k but < $750k: 12% / 9% / 7%.
- Overages after swingline reconciliation billed at 1.25x the blended prepaid unit price (to discourage chronic shortfalls).
- Require renewal notice and utilization review 90 days before tranche renewal.

Operational notes: we should require a monthly usage report from the customer (simple CSV) and a 30-day advance notice to use >50% of swingline capacity in a given quarter. Liability cap for credits = 40% of prepaid tranche (we can tighten to 25% if legal pushes back).

Thanks — approved in principle. A few guardrails before we share externally:

- Limit swingline single-quarter borrow to 20% of that quarter's forecasted consumption; reconcile annually.
- Cap total credit liability to 30% of the prepaid tranche (keeps downside bounded).
- No cash refunds except under explicitly listed failure scenarios; credits only.
- Add a clause that requires Helios to run a quarterly adoption review with our CS team; if adoption drops >40% for two consecutive quarters we reserve the right to reprice the remaining term.

Finance/legal should run the attached pricing model through margin tests (Ben), and ops should confirm we can operationalize monthly CSV reconciliations without manual uplift (Avery). Once legal buys the SOW tweaks, forward to procurement with a 7-day signature window.
